name: authors-integration
description: Messaging and integration principles. Pattern names are used as names; no text reused.

rules.title: Message consumers are idempotent
rules.requirement: Every consumer tolerates receiving the same message more than once without a wrong side effect, and the design names how duplicates are detected, for example a message id store or a natural idempotency key.

rules.title: Poison messages have a dead letter path with an owner
rules.requirement: A message that cannot be processed after bounded retries is moved to a dead letter channel, the design names who watches that channel and how messages are replayed or discarded.

source.name: Gregor Hohpe and Bobby Woolf
source.locator: Enterprise Integration Patterns, Dead Letter Channel and Invalid Message Channel

rules.title: The integration style is chosen deliberately per interaction
rules.requirement: For each interaction the design says whether it is a synchronous call, an asynchronous message or a shared data store, and why that style fits the coupling and timing needs of that interaction.

source.name: Gregor Hohpe and Bobby Woolf
source.locator: Enterprise Integration Patterns, Chapter 2, Integration Styles

rules.title: Message contracts are versioned and evolve compatibly
rules.requirement: Message schemas have a version, additive changes are the norm, consumers ignore unknown fields, and the design states how a breaking change would be rolled out across producers and consumers.

source.name: Gregor Hohpe and Bobby Woolf
source.locator: Enterprise Integration Patterns, Canonical Data Model and Message Translator

rules.title: Database changes and published events are atomic
rules.requirement: Where a service both updates its database and publishes an event, the design prevents one happening without the other, for example through a transactional outbox or change data capture.

rules.title: Long-running processes are modelled as sagas with compensation
rules.requirement: A multi-step business process across services names its steps, the compensating action for each step, and how a partially completed process is detected and resolved.
